paragraphs: A privacy guarantee is useful only if the implemented learning system actually provides it. This paper develops a statistical framework for auditing the privacy behavior of machine learning implementations that claim differential privacy. Its focus is empirical evaluation: examining how much information a particular combination of data, learning algorithm, and privacy specification can reveal.

The framework combines improved methods for searching for privacy leakage and verifying it statistically with poisoning attacks based on influence. These attacks help probe the learner's response to changes in its training data. The combined approach addresses two shortcomings identified in earlier audits: methods tailored to particular models and tests with limited power to detect privacy loss.

The authors report substantially stronger auditing power on logistic regression, Naive Bayes, and random forests. The framework can expose privacy violations caused by implementation mistakes or misuse. When such violations are absent, its measurements can still help characterize information leakage, giving developers an empirical view of the privacy behavior of the system they actually run.
neurips-2022-a-general-framework-for-aud.tldr: A statistical auditing framework uses stronger privacy searches and poisoning attacks to detect privacy leakage across multiple machine learning models.

paragraphs: Offline reinforcement learning must learn useful behavior from an existing dataset. Methods that estimate the value of unfamiliar actions can make evaluation errors, while imitation methods can remain too close to the recorded behavior. Policy-guided Offline RL, or POR, aims to retain the stability of supervised imitation while allowing new combinations of behavior supported by the dataset.

POR separates decision-making into a guide policy and an execution policy. Both are trained separately through supervised learning using only the available data. At evaluation time, the guide tells the execution policy where to go to obtain higher rewards. This division enables composition at the level of states, rather than the action composition used by earlier imitation approaches.

The authors report state-of-the-art performance on the D4RL benchmark. They also highlight improvements from adding suboptimal data and adaptation to new tasks by changing only the guide policy. These findings support the usefulness of separating reward-directed guidance from execution: the same execution component can support different guidance, while additional recorded behavior can expand what the system can compose.
neurips-2022-a-policy-guided-imitation-a.tldr: POR separates guidance from execution to combine stable offline imitation with state-based composition and strong benchmark performance.

paragraphs: Coordinating multiple learning agents becomes awkward when every agent must select actions at the same time. In realistic settings, actions can take different amounts of time, and synchronized decisions require agents to wait and communicate reliably about completion. This paper develops learning methods that allow agents to make decisions asynchronously while using actions that extend over time.

The authors formulate a family of multi-agent actor-critic methods that directly optimize asynchronous policies. They cover three training arrangements: agents learning independently, centralized learning, and centralized training followed by decentralized execution. Addressing all three makes asynchronous decision-making available across different ways of organizing learning and execution, rather than tying it to a single coordination arrangement.

Experiments in both simulation and hardware examine the methods across realistic domains. The authors report superior performance in large multi-agent problems and effective learning of high-quality asynchronous solutions. The contribution is therefore both a formulation of policy optimization for unequal action durations and empirical evidence that agents can learn useful coordinated behavior without requiring synchronized action selection.
neurips-2022-asynchronous-actor-critic-f.tldr: Asynchronous actor-critic methods let multiple agents learn and act with different action durations across three standard training arrangements.

paragraphs: Controlling generated text becomes difficult when the requested property involves detailed structure rather than a broad attribute such as sentiment. This paper targets that problem with Diffusion-LM, a language model designed to make fine-grained control possible through its intermediate representations. The motivation is to steer generation without retraining a language model for each desired behavior.

Diffusion-LM generates text through a non-autoregressive process that repeatedly removes noise from a sequence of Gaussian vectors until it obtains word vectors. This produces a hierarchy of intermediate continuous variables. Because these variables are continuous, a gradient-based algorithm can adjust them during generation to pursue a control objective, making the intermediate generation process an explicit place to apply guidance.

The authors demonstrate successful control on six challenging fine-grained tasks and report substantial improvements over previous work. The findings support the value of a diffusion-based representation for controlling language generation. In particular, the model's sequence of intermediate states provides opportunities to guide complex properties, including the kind of syntactic control that motivates the paper.
neurips-2022-diffusion-lm-improves-contr.tldr: Diffusion-LM uses continuous denoising states to enable gradient-guided text generation with successful fine-grained control on six tasks.

paragraphs: Contrastive learning builds image representations by bringing transformed versions of the same image closer together and separating versions of different images. Energy-Based Contrastive Learning, or EBCLR, combines this objective with energy-based generative modeling. The paper gives the combination a theoretical interpretation as learning the joint distribution of two transformed views of the same image.

The authors evaluate EBCLR on small and medium-scale datasets, including MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100. They report acceleration ranging from fourfold to twentyfold relative to SimCLR and MoCo v2 when measured in training epochs. This result concerns the number of epochs needed in the reported comparisons, rather than a stated measurement of elapsed computing time.

EBCLR also achieves nearly unchanged performance when the number of negative pairs per positive pair falls from 254 to 30, corresponding to batch sizes of 128 and 16. The authors contrast this behavior with SimCLR. Together, the results suggest that combining generative and contrastive learning can reduce dependence on large numbers of negative examples in the studied settings.
neurips-2022-energy-based-contrastive-le.tldr: EBCLR combines contrastive and energy-based learning, reporting fewer training epochs and resilience to smaller negative-pair sets on small and medium-scale datasets.

paragraphs: Graph neural networks used in materials science often borrow their structure from models of molecules. This paper argues that crystals have additional organization that these models do not exploit. It introduces networks designed around crystalline symmetry groups, so the model's computations respond consistently to the transformations described by those groups.

The central change is a generalization of message passing, the operation through which nodes in a graph exchange information. The proposed operation can work with more general permutation groups, allowing the architecture to incorporate crystal-specific symmetry. The authors also describe it as an expressive convolution on the crystal graph, providing another way to understand how local information is combined within the structured material.

On the Materials Project dataset, the models achieve results competitive with state-of-the-art approaches. This empirical finding supports incorporating crystalline structure directly into a learning architecture. The contribution connects a mathematical description of crystal symmetries to practical graph computations, showing that such structure can be used in models that remain competitive on materials prediction.
neurips-2022-equivariant-networks-for-cr.tldr: Crystal-aware message passing builds symmetry-equivariant networks that achieve competitive results on the Materials Project dataset.

paragraphs: FocalNets replace self-attention entirely with a different mechanism for exchanging information between visual tokens. The proposed focal modulation module first builds contextual information at several ranges, then selects useful context for each token, and finally uses that context to modify the token's representation. The aim is effective visual modeling at computational costs similar to attention-based alternatives.

The module uses a stack of depth-wise convolutions to gather context from nearby and more distant regions. Gates select which contextual information matters for each query token based on its content. An element-wise modulation or affine transformation then combines the selected context with the query. These stages separate constructing context, selecting it, and applying it.

Experiments show improvements over self-attention counterparts, including Swin and Focal Transformers, on classification, detection, and segmentation. Tiny and base FocalNets reach 82.3% and 83.9% ImageNet-1K top-1 accuracy. In the reported Mask R-CNN comparison, a base FocalNet with a shorter training schedule also surpasses a Swin model trained with a longer schedule. The results support focal modulation as a practical alternative across several vision tasks.
neurips-2022-focal-modulation-networks-d.tldr: FocalNets replace self-attention with selective multiscale context modulation and outperform attention-based counterparts across several vision benchmarks.

paragraphs: A model trained from examples may still produce outputs that violate requirements imposed by its application. A concurrent verifier checks an input-output pair and modifies the output to meet those requirements. This paper studies what happens to learning and generalization when such a verifier becomes part of the prediction system.

The analysis asks how adding the verifier changes learnability and whether it must participate during training. The authors establish a condition under which a guaranteed hypothesis can be obtained while using the verifier only at inference time. This is a conditional result: it identifies circumstances in which verification can be attached to prediction without needing to be used throughout learning.

For multi-class classification and structured prediction, the authors also show that typical error bounds based on Rademacher complexity do not become larger when a concurrent verifier is used. This connects output certification to statistical generalization analysis. The finding concerns the stated theoretical bounds, giving a reason that enforcing requirements through a verifier need not worsen those bounds in the analyzed settings.
neurips-2022-generalization-analysis-on-.tldr: The paper identifies conditions for inference-time verification guarantees and shows that standard complexity-based error bounds need not increase.

paragraphs: Streaming speech recognition must produce predictions as speech arrives, and its word error rate can lag behind that of non-streaming systems. This paper introduces the Globally Normalized Autoregressive Transducer, or GNAT, to address label bias in streaming recognition. Its central modeling choice is to normalize scores at the level of complete sequences.

Sequence-level normalization requires computing a denominator that accounts for the sequence alternatives. GNAT makes that computation both exact and tractable. The model is developed within a modular framework encompassing common neural speech recognition models, allowing modeling decisions to be varied in a controlled way and providing a basis for constructing additional models.

Through theory and experiments, the authors show that global normalization can substantially narrow the streaming versus non-streaming performance gap. On Librispeech, the reported reduction in the word error rate gap exceeds 50%; this describes a reduction in the gap, rather than a halving of streaming error itself. The contribution combines a usable normalization method with a framework for examining the consequences of speech-model design choices.
neurips-2022-global-normalization-for-st.tldr: GNAT makes exact global normalization tractable and reduces the streaming versus non-streaming word error rate gap by over 50% on Librispeech.

paragraphs: HSurf-Net estimates surface normals from three-dimensional point clouds affected by noise and uneven sampling density. Earlier approaches fit local geometric surfaces using polynomials of a predefined order. The paper identifies a weakness in that choice: an unsuitable polynomial order or outlying points can make the fitted surface too simple or too sensitive to the observations.

The proposed method learns surface patterns implicitly in a higher-dimensional feature space. Multilayer perceptrons represent these patterns, while a space transformation module combines local aggregation and global shifts to learn the feature space. Relative position encoding maps the points into that space. The model then predicts normal vectors directly from the learned surface features.

The surface representation and transformation modules are optimized together, allowing the model to adapt its surface patterns to different points. Experiments report state-of-the-art performance on synthetic shapes and real indoor and outdoor scenes. These results support replacing a fixed polynomial surface choice with a learned representation when estimating normals under the noise and density variations considered in the paper.
neurips-2022-hsurf-net-normal-estimation.tldr: HSurf-Net learns implicit surface patterns in feature space to estimate point-cloud normals under noise and density variation.

paragraphs: This paper explains image-model predictions by measuring statistical dependence between input regions and model outputs. Its attribution method uses the Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion, or HSIC, with kernel representations of distributions. This provides a way to assign importance to image regions while treating the prediction model as a black box.

The authors emphasize that HSIC can be estimated efficiently. In their experiments, the method is up to eight times faster than previous leading black-box attribution methods while retaining comparable faithfulness. Across several fidelity metrics on ImageNet and multiple recent architectures, it matches or improves on leading black-box and white-box attribution approaches. The method also extends to explaining object detectors such as YOLOv4.

A further contribution is a kernel that separates importance scores into components in an ANOVA-like decomposition. This allows the method to assess both individual image patches and pairwise interactions between patches. The explanation can therefore describe contributions associated with combinations of regions, expanding the information available beyond a collection of separate patch importance scores.
neurips-2022-making-sense-of-dependence-.tldr: HSIC-based attribution efficiently explains image predictions and can separate individual patch importance from pairwise interactions.

paragraphs: This paper examines learning dynamics in quantum zero-sum games, extending a line of analysis previously developed for classical games. Its motivation includes growing interest in quantum computing and quantum generative adversarial networks. The focus is on how players' selected quantum states evolve when their choices are governed by particular learning rules.

The authors study Matrix Multiplicative Weights Update and its continuous counterpart, Quantum Replicator Dynamics. For players following the continuous dynamics, they establish conservation laws expressed in quantum-information terms. These laws identify quantities that remain preserved as the players' states change, providing mathematical structure for understanding the resulting joint evolution.

The system also exhibits Poincare recurrence: almost all trajectories return arbitrarily close to their starting conditions infinitely many times. This describes repeated near-returns, without requiring every trajectory to repeat exactly or follow a fixed period. The results generalize earlier classical-game findings to the quantum setting and characterize persistent behavior of the learning dynamics, rather than presenting them simply as a route to a settled state.
neurips-2022-matrix-multiplicative-weigh.tldr: Quantum replicator dynamics in quantum zero-sum games obey conservation laws and exhibit recurrence for almost all trajectories.

paragraphs: Neural Motion Fields, or NeMF, represent kinematic motion as a continuous function of time. Instead of making a sequence of discrete motion samples the central representation, the method learns a neural function that describes motion across time. This gives generation and editing tasks a shared representation of the underlying motion space.

The generative network takes a time coordinate and a random latent vector that controls motion style. It is trained as a variational autoencoder, with motion encoders supporting sampling in the latent space. These inputs separate the point in time being represented from the style of the generated motion, allowing a learned motion field to describe different motions within the same model.

The authors train on diverse human motions and on a quadruped dataset to demonstrate versatility. They then use the representation as a general motion prior for applications including interpolation, in-betweening, and re-navigation, reporting superiority in different generation and editing tasks. The findings support continuous motion fields as a reusable basis for several animation operations.
neurips-2022-nemf-neural-motion-fields-f.tldr: NeMF learns continuous, style-conditioned motion fields that serve as a shared prior for motion generation and editing.

paragraphs: Bilevel optimization nests one optimization problem inside another, making even gradient-based learning potentially expensive. Computing the outer problem's hypergradient can involve costly second-order derivative operations. This paper investigates Hessian-free alternatives and reports that approximating the entire hypergradient can introduce substantial variance and unstable training.

The proposed method approximates only the response Jacobian, the component describing how the inner solution responds to changes in the outer variables. It estimates that response by taking the difference between two optimization trajectories. The authors analyze the estimator's approximation quality and smoothness despite its dependence on those trajectories, obtaining the first known convergence-rate result for this type of Hessian-free bilevel algorithm.

Experiments report improvements over baseline bilevel optimizers across several problems. In few-shot meta-learning with ResNet-12 on miniImageNet, the method outperforms baseline meta-learning algorithms, while other tested bilevel optimizers do not solve the problem within comparable time. The findings favor a more targeted approximation strategy and connect its empirical effectiveness to a convergence analysis.
neurips-2022-on-the-convergence-theory-f.tldr: A Hessian-free bilevel method estimates only the response Jacobian through two optimization paths, with convergence guarantees and favorable empirical results.

paragraphs: Online learning requires decisions to be updated as examples arrive. This paper studies an adversary that can adapt its sampling distribution over time but cannot concentrate it arbitrarily: its density is bounded by 1/σ times the uniform density. This smoothing assumption creates a setting between unrestricted adversarial inputs and a fixed data distribution.

Given access to an offline empirical-risk-minimization oracle, the authors construct computationally efficient online algorithms with sublinear regret controlled by class complexity and smoothness. For T rounds and dimension d, the bounds scale as the square root of T d/σ for real-valued functions and the square root of T d/√σ for binary-valued functions. Thus, stronger concentration allowances worsen the stated guarantees.

Under this framework, the results establish that efficient offline optimization can support efficient online learning, contrasting with the computational separation under worst-case adversaries. The paper additionally improves oracle-efficient regret bounds for binary-valued functions in finite-domain and transductive worst-case settings. The main equivalence remains tied to the specified smoothing assumption and access to the offline oracle.
neurips-2022-oracle-efficient-online-lea.tldr: With bounded-density adversarial sampling and an offline optimization oracle, online learning admits efficient algorithms with dimension-dependent sublinear regret.

paragraphs: Neural fields offer compact signal representations that are easy to optimize, but treating the learned representation as a black box makes many forms of signal editing difficult. This paper introduces basis-encoded polynomial neural fields, or PNFs, to expose interpretable components within the representation. The aim is to preserve the advantages of neural fields while making their contents manipulable.

A PNF represents a signal through a composition of components that can be examined and changed. The authors develop a general theoretical framework for analyzing and designing these fields, then use it to construct Fourier PNFs. This links the architecture's internal organization to the goal of manipulating parts of the represented signal.

Fourier PNFs match state-of-the-art performance on signal representation tasks using neural fields. Experiments also demonstrate texture transfer and scale-space interpolation. Together, these results show that the proposed structure can support editing operations while retaining competitive representation quality, making manipulation part of the representation's design rather than leaving the learned signal entirely opaque.
neurips-2022-polynomial-neural-fields-fo.tldr: Polynomial neural fields expose interpretable signal components, enabling manipulation while matching leading neural-field representation performance.

paragraphs: Conventional graph neural networks repeatedly aggregate neighboring information, a process related to the one-dimensional Weisfeiler-Lehman test. This paper identifies redundant message flows in that process as an obstacle to carrying information along longer paths and learning graph similarities. Its proposed Redundancy-Free Graph Neural Network, or RFGNN, changes how path information reaches the representation.

RFGNN propagates information from each original-graph path, up to a limited length, through a single message flow. The authors theoretically show greater expressive power than the one-dimensional Weisfeiler-Lehman test and efficient propagation of graph structure that avoids the over-squashing issue in their analysis. The architecture also captures subgraphs at multiple levels of detail.

The analysis further indicates that graphs with closer graph edit distances are more likely to receive similar representations. This connects structural resemblance to the geometry of the learned encoding without claiming an exact correspondence for every graph pair. Graph-level prediction experiments support the theoretical assertions, with RFGNN achieving the best reported results on most of the evaluated datasets.
neurips-2022-redundancy-free-message-pas.tldr: RFGNN removes redundant path message flows, improving theoretical expressiveness and achieving leading results on most evaluated graph prediction datasets.

paragraphs: Federated learning systems often deploy models as though participating devices had similar computing resources. When hardware differs, choosing a complex model can restrict access to data held by less capable clients. This paper introduces All-In-One Neural Composition to support models whose computational complexity can adapt to each client's available resources.

The mechanism constructs models of different complexities from a unified neural basis shared across clients. Its soft, learnable extraction of smaller models generalizes pruning-based approaches, which derive local models by removing parts of a global model. The shared basis provides a common foundation for learning while allowing participating devices to work with different model sizes.

The resulting system, FLANC, is evaluated on federated learning benchmarks with varied hardware and data heterogeneity. The authors report consistent performance gains while maintaining high computation and communication efficiency. These findings support adapting the model construction process to client resources as a way to use knowledge distributed across devices without imposing a uniform model complexity on all participants.
neurips-2022-resource-adaptive-federated.tldr: FLANC composes resource-adapted client models from a shared neural basis, improving performance across heterogeneous federated learning settings.

paragraphs: Streaming principal component analysis seeks principal directions from data arriving over time. Standard analyses assume that the data-generating covariance stays fixed. This paper instead considers a perturbed stochastic model in which the covariance belongs to an uncertainty set that varies over time, making uncertainty in the evolving data distribution part of the problem.

Within this setting, the authors derive fundamental limits on recovering principal components. Such limits establish what any algorithm can achieve under the model, providing a reference for judging particular methods. They then analyze the convergence of the noisy power method and Oja's algorithm, both of which have also been studied under stationary data generation.

The authors argue that the noisy power method achieves an optimal rate in their robust setting and present numerical experiments supporting the analysis. The significance is that performance is assessed against the difficulty imposed by temporal covariance uncertainty itself. This gives both a characterization of the recovery problem and an analysis of established algorithms when the fixed-covariance assumption is relaxed.
neurips-2022-robust-streaming-pca-6c9bbe.tldr: The paper derives recovery limits for streaming PCA with time-varying covariance uncertainty and argues that the noisy power method is rate-optimal.

paragraphs: In sequential games with imperfect information, players must learn while observing only part of what happens. This paper studies extensive-form correlated equilibrium, a solution concept for multiplayer games with potentially different objectives. Its main contribution is an algorithm that learns such an equilibrium efficiently from repeated play, using bandit feedback instead of full game feedback.

The authors introduce K-EFCE, which allows a player to observe and deviate from recommendations K times. The usual equilibrium appears at K = 1, while larger K imposes stronger requirements. Their uncoupled no-regret algorithm accounts for possible recommendation histories when minimizing regret at each information set, the collection of situations a player cannot distinguish.

For approximation error ε, the full-feedback iteration bound scales, up to logarithmic factors, as the largest X_i A_i^K/ε² across players. The bandit version uses X_i A_i^(K+1)/ε² episodes, where X_i and A_i count information sets and actions. Setting K = 1 yields the stated first sample-efficient bandit-feedback algorithm for EFCE, while the dependence on K quantifies the cost of stronger equilibrium requirements.
neurips-2022-sample-efficient-learning-o.tldr: A sample-based no-regret algorithm efficiently learns extensive-form correlated equilibria from bandit feedback, with extensions to stronger recommendation-deviation guarantees.

paragraphs: Federated learning can place heavy demands on communication, especially in wireless settings. Compressing exchanged information helps address that cost, but incorporating privacy protection creates an additional design problem. This paper develops SoteriaFL, a framework that brings communication compression and local differential privacy into the same federated learning procedure.

The authors first examine directly compressing updates from differentially private stochastic gradient descent and identify limitations of that simple combination. SoteriaFL supports a broader family of local gradient estimators, including stochastic variance-reduced methods, together with shifted compression. This allows the analysis to consider several ways of estimating and communicating learning updates within one framework.

The paper characterizes trade-offs among privacy, learning utility, and communication complexity. It shows that SoteriaFL can improve communication complexity over private federated algorithms without compression while preserving privacy and utility in the analyzed comparison. The contribution is a coordinated treatment of these objectives, showing how communication savings can be obtained alongside privacy protection rather than treating their interaction as an afterthought.
neurips-2022-soteriafl-a-unified-framewo.tldr: SoteriaFL combines local differential privacy with communication compression and establishes improved communication complexity without sacrificing the analyzed privacy or utility.

paragraphs: Spartan trains neural networks to meet a predetermined sparsity level, meaning that a specified share of parameters is inactive. The challenge is to decide which parameters to retain while also learning their values. Spartan approaches these decisions together, allowing the sparsity pattern to change during training before increasingly concentrating on a more fixed selection.

The method combines a soft top-k mask derived from regularized optimal transportation with dual-averaging parameter updates and hard sparsification during the forward pass. Early training can explore different masks. Gradually sharpening the soft selection shifts attention toward optimizing the retained parameters. The approach supports individual or block sparsity, global or per-layer budgets, and allocation based on linear models of parameter costs.

On ImageNet-1K, Spartan produces 95% sparse ResNet-50 models and 90% block-sparse ViT-B/16 models with absolute top-1 accuracy losses below one percentage point relative to dense training. These results show that the reported networks can retain much of their classification accuracy under substantial sparsity, while the allocation framework accommodates several ways of specifying the sparsity budget.
neurips-2022-spartan-differentiable-spar.tldr: Spartan learns sparse parameter selections during training, achieving high ResNet and ViT sparsity with less than one percentage point of reported accuracy loss.

paragraphs: When optimization variables represent geometric vectors, rotating the starting problem should ideally rotate the optimized result in the corresponding way. This paper shows that standard Adam does not have that property. Its separate moment updates for individual coordinates can make optimization depend on the coordinate axes, producing noticeable artifacts and biases in geometric applications.

VectorAdam modifies Adam to account for the vector structure of its variables. This makes the optimizer rotation-equivariant when viewed as a mapping from initial conditions to optimized results. The change addresses the optimization procedure itself: even if geometric data are naturally organized as vectors, the update rule must also respect that organization to preserve the desired rotational behavior.

The authors demonstrate VectorAdam on both machine learning and traditional geometry optimization problems. In these experiments, it resolves the artifacts and biases associated with applying conventional Adam to vector-valued data, while matching or improving convergence rates. The results show that respecting geometric structure in an optimizer can improve its behavior without requiring slower convergence in the reported applications.
neurips-2022-vectoradam-for-rotation-equ.tldr: VectorAdam makes Adam respect rotations of vector-valued parameters, removing reported geometric artifacts while matching or improving convergence.

paragraphs: A network can resist adversarial perturbations on its training examples yet remain vulnerable on new data. This paper investigates that gap through expressive power: whether a model is large enough to represent a classifier that generalizes robustly. Its theoretical setting concerns binary classification with well-separated data.

For ReLU networks, the authors show a separation between the size needed for robust training accuracy and robust generalization. Mild overparameterization suffices for high robust training accuracy, while their lower-bound result gives a constant robust generalization gap unless network size is exponential in data dimension. The result extends to linearly separable data and to parameterized function classes whose VC dimension grows at most polynomially with parameter count.

When data lie on a manifold of intrinsic dimension k, the authors provide an improved network-size upper bound exponential in k rather than the ambient dimension. An accompanying lower bound still grows exponentially in k. These results identify representational capacity as a possible source of robust generalization difficulty, including settings where ordinary generalization is easy, and show why lower intrinsic dimension helps without eliminating the theoretical dimensionality barrier.
neurips-2022-why-robust-generalization-i.tldr: Theoretical bounds reveal an exponential model-size separation between robust training and robust generalization in the studied classification settings.

paragraphs: Relative positional encodings tell a Transformer about distances between tokens, but this paper shows that such information does not automatically give the model universal approximation power. The authors identify continuous sequence-to-sequence functions that the analyzed RPE-based Transformers cannot approximate, even when their depth and width are increased arbitrarily.

A key obstruction comes from putting relative positional information inside softmax attention. The resulting attention matrix has rows that sum to one, a constraint that can restrict how the network uses positional information. The authors derive sufficient conditions for universal function approximation and design Universal RPE-based Attention, or URPE Attention, to satisfy those conditions.

The resulting URPE-based Transformers are universal approximators under the theoretical formulation. Experiments across typical architectures and tasks also show parameter efficiency and improvements over strong baselines in a broad range of applications. These are complementary findings: the theory addresses which functions the architecture can represent, while the experiments assess the practical performance of the proposed attention module.
neurips-2022-your-transformer-may-not-be.tldr: URPE Attention addresses a positional-information bottleneck in RPE Transformers and satisfies sufficient conditions for universal sequence-to-sequence approximation.
